correctness.rationale: The source gives all vertices and facets of the canonical polar pair. Every vertex of C_d+Diamond_d is a signed permutation of (2,1,...,1), hence has norm sqrt(d+3). Every sign-vector facet with support k has offset k+1 and normal norm sqrt(k), giving the strict distance shells. Polarity turns the equiradial vertices into equally distant signohedron facets. The source polar vertices have norm sqrt(k)/(k+1), which is strictly decreasing in k. Antipodal facet and vertex pairs prove all four extremal centers are uniquely the origin. The finite verifier independently checks facet ranks and solves both Chebyshev LPs through d=7.

value.rationale: The signohedron is the canonical new combinatorial type arising from generic monotone paths on cross-polytopes. The theorem gives a complete Euclidean metric profile of the source canonical realization in every dimension: all d2^d facets are simultaneously tangent, all 3^d-1 vertices split into exactly d strict radial shells with closed multiplicities, and the polar partner has the reciprocal strict facet shells. This is structural family-wide information not encoded by the previously studied face lattice or flip graph.
